calls.prompt:
Company: CornerCare Pharmacy

US drugstore chain with 300 neighborhood pharmacies in the Midwest (~6,000 employees). Fills prescriptions (including controlled painkillers and ADHD medicines), gives flu and COVID shots, and sells over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, snacks and household goods. Most prescriptions are paid by Medicare, Medicaid or private insurance. No hospitals or clinics, does not make any drugs, no mail-order.

Rules that APPLY:
- DEA rules for pharmacies that dispense controlled substances (registration, opioids, telehealth prescribing)
- FDA rules on over-the-counter drugs, drug labeling, drug shortages and recalls that reach pharmacy shelves
- Medicare Part D and Medicaid payment and pharmacy rules (CMS)
- CDC vaccine recommendations that change what pharmacists may give
- Patient privacy (HIPAA) and pharmacy recordkeeping
- Workplace and labor rules for retail stores

Rules that DO NOT apply:
- Approval, manufacturing or inspection rules aimed only at drug or device manufacturers
- Hospital, nursing-home, physician-payment or clinical-lab rules
- Research grants, clinical trials, NIH funding notices
- Banking, securities, aviation, energy, farming

Affected areas and owners:
- pharmacy-ops: Dispensing, controlled substances (DEA), pharmacist scope, vaccines → Priya Raman (Pharmacy Operations)
- drug-safety: OTC products, labeling, recalls, shortages (FDA) → Daniel Brooks (Drug Safety & Quality)
- payers: Medicare Part D, Medicaid and insurer billing (CMS) → Lucia Moreno (Reimbursement)
- privacy-people: Patient privacy (HIPAA), records, store workforce → Sam Whitaker (Privacy & HR Compliance)

Task: Find every US Federal Register document published between 2026-11-09 and 2026-11-13 (inclusive) that affects this company. For each, give the Federal Register document number, title, federalregister.gov URL, the key deadline, a tier (Critical if it is a rule or proposed rule with a deadline less than 90 days after 2026-11-13, or a final rule that took effect within the 30 days before 2026-11-13; otherwise High for final rules, Medium for proposed rules and for notices with a deadline, Low for anything else), the owner area, a one-line reason, and a one-line action. Only include items you found via search. Return an empty list if none.
calls.output:
I found one Federal Register document in the 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-13 window that affects CornerCare. My search tool couldn't list every document published that week, so this may not be complete.

## Items

**1. 2026-22792 — Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program and Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Program (final rule, published 2026-11-09)**
- **URL:** https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/09/2026-22792/medicare-drug-price-negotiation-program-and-medicare-prescription-drug-benefit-program
- **Key deadline:** The regulations are effective on December 5, 2026. That is 22 days after 2026-11-13.
- **Tier:** Critical. It is a rule with a deadline under 90 days out.
- **Owner area:** payers (Lucia Moreno, Reimbursement)
- **Reason:** The rule finalizes and codifies the Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program and sets new Part D policies. It covers how the negotiated price paid to a network pharmacy is reported at the point of sale, which affects CornerCare's Part D reimbursement.
- **Action:** Reimbursement should review the final text for pharmacy payment, point-of-sale pricing and claims-reporting changes. It should update billing and contract workflows before the Dec 5 effective date, and brief store pharmacy teams on any changes to claim handling for negotiated-price drugs.

## Reviewed and left out
- **2026-22812 (Nov 10), CMS "CARE" proposed rule:** It revises conditions of participation for hospitals, long-term care and similar facilities. The small entities it names are small hospitals, critical access hospitals, long-term care facilities, and intermediate care facilities. That is outside CornerCare's scope.
- **2026-22843 (Nov 10), proposed 2027 aggregate production quotas, and 2026-22842 (Nov 10), 2026 quota adjustment:** These are DEA quota actions aimed at manufacturers. I left them out under your exclusion for manufacturing rules. Pharmacy Operations and Drug Safety may still want to watch them. The adjustment raises the 2026 quotas for d,l-amphetamine, d-amphetamine, hydromorphone and methylphenidate. The proposed 2027 quotas also cover the assessment of annual needs for ephedrine, pseudoephedrine, and phenylpropanolamine. I did not confirm a comment deadline for 2026-22843.
- **2026-22996 (Nov 12) and 2026-22965 (Nov 12), FDA notices:** One is a request for information on real-world data in drug and biologic submissions. The other is an information collection for the Voluntary Qualified Importer Program. Both are aimed at manufacturers and importers, so I excluded them.
- **DEA 7-hydroxymitragynine/mitragynine pseudoindoxyl temporary scheduling order:** The order was set to be published on or after November 13, 2026. One source dated Nov 13 says no temporary scheduling order for 7-OH had been published as of November 13, 2026. I found no in-window publication, so I did not list it.
- **Items published outside the window:** The HIPAA Privacy Rule final rule (2026-23429) was published Nov 19. The CMS Part D pharmacy contracting RFI was published Sept 24. The CMS PBM proposed rule (2026-21420) was published Oct 20. None falls in the Nov 9–13 window.

markdown:
# Regulatory triage — CornerCare Pharmacy
Window 2026-11-09 → 2026-11-13 · as of 2026-11-13 · 1 items

## Critical (1)

- **Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program and Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Program** [web search — verify]
  - Lucia Moreno (Reimbursement) should review the final text for pharmacy payment, point-of-sale pricing and claims-reporting changes, update billing and contract workflows before the Dec 5 effective date, and brief store pharmacy teams on claim handling for negotiated-price drugs.
  - Deadline: 2026-12-05 (effective, quoted ✓) · Owner: Lucia Moreno (Reimbursement) · Areas: payers
  - 91 FR 72176 ✓ · https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/09/2026-22792/medicare-drug-price-negotiation-program-and-medicare-prescription-drug-benefit-program

votes.why: Plain English with a concrete lead step (review the final text for pharmacy payment and pricing changes), though it bundles several follow-on tasks.
Setting Dec 5 as the deadline for billing and contract updates implies a Dec 5, 2026 compliance date, which the rubric forbids, and briefing stores on claim handling suggests new store duties.
Omits the maximum fair price plus dispensing fee cap, the sales tax and vaccine fee inclusion, and the January 1, 2029 applicability date.
It gives Lucia three tasks—review the rule, update workflows, and brief pharmacy teams—instead of one concrete next step.
Directing workflow updates before December 5 implies an unsupported compliance deadline; the rubric places the Part D coverage changes on January 1, 2029.

It omits the selected-drug payment cap at the maximum fair price plus dispensing fees, the inclusion of sales tax and vaccine administration fees in the negotiated price, and the January 1, 2029 Part D coverage start.
The action bundles three separate tasks (reviewing text, updating workflows, and briefing store teams) rather than naming one concrete next step.
The action violates the rubric by claiming workflows must be updated before a December 5 compliance date and implying new store pharmacy claim-handling duties.
The action omits all three required points: the maximum fair price plus dispensing fee cap, inclusion of sales tax and vaccine fees in negotiated price, and the January 1, 2029 applicability date.
